a171.speaker: Nationwide survey presented by Dr. Greg Mills and Hon. Tendai Biti, former Zimbabwean Finance Minister, of the Platform of African Democrats (PAD)
a171.name: Nationwide survey presented by Dr. Greg Mills and Hon. Tendai Biti
a171.title: former Zimbabwean Finance Minister, of the Platform of African Democrats (PAD)
a171.speech: According to the survey of 1,000 registered voters conducted between January 24 and February 6, 2025, 89 percent of Malawians believe the country is headed in the wrong direction; over 71% said their lives have worsened over the past five years; 84% describe the country's economic situation as "bad," with 74% calling it "very bad"; over 80% report going hungry in the past year and 60% went without access to medicines or treatment; nearly 40% have witnessed corruption by government officials in the last 12 months; more than three-quarters of voters said President Chakwera has performed worse than former President Arthur Peter Mutharika; 91% say they do not trust the current administration; 86% believe the government cannot create jobs or feed people; 70% say the government has made no progress since 2020; and 79% believe Malawi must stop begging for foreign aid and instead chart a self-reliant path forward.

a171.speaker: One analyst at the survey launch (unnamed)
a171.name: One analyst at the survey launch (unnamed)
a171.speech: "This is not just a downturn — it's a breakdown," warning that the data reflects an urgent humanitarian and political crisis.

a171.speaker: Report authors (Platform of African Democrats study)
a171.name: Report authors (Platform of African Democrats study)
a171.speech: "The crisis is here. The time to act is now. Elections should not be an excuse for inertia, but a mandate for real change." The study concludes with a 12-point action plan urging leaders to embrace urgent reforms, manage elite interests, build institutions, and abandon the politics of rent-seeking and patronage.

a236.speaker: SaharaReporters (prior reporting)
a236.name: SaharaReporters (prior reporting)
a236.speech: Reported earlier that suspected political thugs allegedly mobilised by the Ekiti State government and legal luminary, Afe Babalola, SAN, had gathered around the Magistrate Court premises, allegedly intimidating those in attendance.

a236.speaker: Sahara Reporters (@SaharaReporters), social media post
a236.name: Sahara Reporters (@SaharaReporters)
a236.title: social media post
a236.speech: "WATCH: How DSS Operatives Escorted Political Thugs To Attack Activists During @DeleFarotimi's Trial In Ekiti"

a236.speaker: Ado-Ekiti Magistrate Court, Ekiti State (court record)
a236.name: Ado-Ekiti Magistrate Court
a236.title: Ekiti State (court record)
a236.speech: Reserved its ruling and adjourned the bail application of human rights lawyer, Dele Farotimi, to Friday, December 20, 2024, meaning Farotimi will remain in custody for another 10 days.

a236.speaker: Dele Farotimi, human rights lawyer (defendant)
a236.name: Dele Farotimi
a236.title: human rights lawyer (defendant)
a236.speech: Pleaded not guilty to 14 charges levelled against him at the Ekiti State Magistrate Court.

a236.speaker: Dele Farotimi, human rights lawyer (preliminary objection filed through lead counsel Adeyinka Olumide-Fusika, SAN)
a236.name: Dele Farotimi
a236.title: human rights lawyer (preliminary objection filed through lead counsel Adeyinka Olumide-Fusika, SAN)
a236.speech: Submitted a preliminary objection, urging the Ado Ekiti Magistrate Court to dismiss the defamation suit filed against him by Afe Babalola (SAN), arguing that the charge against him is legally invalid, non-existent, and that the magistrate acted beyond their jurisdiction by considering an incompetent charge ; "The 16-count charge before the magistrate court pertains to alleged offences under the 'Criminal Code Act.' The Criminal Code Act is applicable in Ekiti State through adoption and/or domestication as the Criminal Code Law, Cap. C16, Laws of Ekiti, 2012. The Criminal Code Law, Cap. C16, Laws of Ekiti, 2012 has been expressly repealed and replaced by Section 429(a) of the Criminal Law of Ekiti State, 2021. The alleged defamation of Aare Afe Babalola, SAN, and two of his partners, Olu Daramola, SAN, Olu Faro, as well as the law firm Afe Babalola & Co., as detailed in the charges, is not recognised under the Criminal Law of Ekiti State, 2021, and is, therefore, non-existent. Based on these points, the Honourable Magistrate acted without jurisdiction by allowing the charge to proceed, ordering the arraignment of the defendant, and subsequently ordering his detention in prison."

a236.speaker: Prosecution (Ekiti State Magistrate Court)
a236.name: Prosecution (Ekiti State Magistrate Court)
a236.speech: Amended and reduced the charges from 16 to 14 before serving them to the defendant.

a247.speaker: Kingdom of Morocco (official position at the Paris conference)
a247.name: Kingdom of Morocco (official position at the Paris conference)
a247.speech: Morocco called on Thursday for an immediate and complete ceasefire in Lebanon, at an international conference in Paris, calling for respect for the nation's sovereignty and the dignity of its people.

a247.speaker: Fouad Yazourh, Morocco's ambassador and director general of bilateral relations at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a247.name: Fouad Yazourh
a247.title: Morocco's ambassador and director general of bilateral relations at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a247.speech: Speaking on behalf of Morocco, stressed that Lebanon should not continue to suffer from conflicts fuelled by regional agendas ; "Lebanon cannot and must not continue to bear the burden of conflicts taking place elsewhere," adding that these conflicts have exhausted the country ; expressed Morocco's support for immediate international action, calling on the United Nations to supervise a ceasefire and facilitate the return of displaced persons with guarantees of protection ; stressed the need for the Lebanese authorities to manage humanitarian aid, alongside international efforts to rebuild the country ; reiterated Morocco's solidarity with Lebanon, calling for "reason and diplomacy to prevail," and called for a simultaneous political approach, alongside the ceasefire, to establish a just and stable peace in the Middle East.

a247.speaker: Fouad Yazourh, Morocco's ambassador and director general of bilateral relations at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a247.name: Fouad Yazourh
a247.title: Morocco's ambassador and director general of bilateral relations at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
a247.speech: Recalled that Morocco, led by King Mohammed VI, has advocated a comprehensive solution to the region's crisis; stressed that the Palestinian question was at the heart of the broader Middle East conflict, reiterating Morocco's long-standing position that a two-State solution is essential for lasting peace ; "An independent Palestine, with Gaza as an integral part and East Jerusalem as its capital, is necessary for any lasting security in the region."

a247.speaker: King Mohammed VI of Morocco
a247.name: King Mohammed VI of Morocco
a247.speech: His constant message that without a resolution of the Palestinian question, tensions will persist.

a317.speaker: Constitutional Court of South Africa (judgment delivered in Johannesburg)
a317.name: Constitutional Court of South Africa (judgment delivered in Johannesburg)
a317.speech: Ruled that men can now legally adopt their wives' surnames, striking down sections of the Births and Deaths Registration Act that had restricted surname changes to women, declaring the provisions unconstitutional and affirming that equality before the law applies to both genders.

a317.speaker: Durban man who brought the case
a317.name: Durban man who brought the case
a317.speech: Argued that the law discriminated against men, denying them the same rights that women had long exercised.

a317.speaker: Rights groups
a317.name: Rights groups
a317.speech: Celebrated the ruling as a step toward dismantling patriarchal traditions embedded in legislation.

a317.speaker: Bheki Simelane, elder in Mbabane
a317.name: Bheki Simelane
a317.title: elder in Mbabane
a317.speech: “In our culture, a surname is not just paperwork. It connects you to your ancestors.” ; “For a man to give up his surname is to give up himself. That is not something we can accept.”

a317.speaker: Sipho Dlamini, 34-year-old accountant in Manzini
a317.name: Sipho Dlamini
a317.title: 34-year-old accountant in Manzini
a317.speech: “If a man loves his wife enough to carry her name, I see no problem. At the end of the day, it's just a name. What matters is how you live.”

a317.speaker: Nondumiso Khumalo, nurse in Ezulwini
a317.name: Nondumiso Khumalo
a317.title: nurse in Ezulwini
a317.speech: “For centuries, women have been expected to abandon their identity the moment they marry.” ; “Now men can also make that choice. That is fairness.”

a317.speaker: Gugu Mamba, shop owner in Mbabane
a317.name: Gugu Mamba
a317.title: shop owner in Mbabane
a317.speech: “Marriage here is not just between two people but two families. That is why a woman takes her husband's surname. For a man to do the same makes no sense in our way of life.”

a317.speaker: Thuli Mavuso, attorney
a317.name: Thuli Mavuso
a317.title: attorney
a317.speech: Noted that nothing explicitly prevents a man from taking his wife's surname, but that such an application would likely raise eyebrows: “There is no written ban, but because it goes against custom and practice, officials may hesitate to register it.”

a317.speaker: Mcebo Magagula, constitutional scholar
a317.name: Mcebo Magagula
a317.title: constitutional scholar
a317.speech: Argued that the South African reasoning could resonate locally if tested in court: “Our Constitution guarantees equality, but judges are always cautious where custom is concerned. It would be a difficult, but important, case.”

a317.speaker: Andile Shongwe, law student at the University of Eswatini
a317.name: Andile Shongwe
a317.title: law student at the University of Eswatini
a317.speech: “This is not just about names. It is about gender roles. For too long, only women had to adjust their identity for marriage. South Africa has said men can now do the same. That symbolism is powerful.”

a317.speaker: Ndumiso Mdluli, Deputy Senate President of Eswatini
a317.name: Ndumiso Mdluli
a317.title: Deputy Senate President of Eswatini
a317.speech: Emphasised that surnames are integral to rituals and responsibilities: “When a man abandons his surname, who will speak for him at the family kraal? Who will bury him? These are not small matters.”

a317.speaker: Government officials in Eswatini (non-response)
a317.name: Government officials in Eswatini (non-response)
a317.speech: Declined to say whether they would approve a man's request to adopt his wife's surname.

a317.speaker: Senior government officer in Eswatini (anonymous)
a317.name: Senior government officer in Eswatini (anonymous)
a317.speech: Admitted that no such application had been processed “in recent memory.”

a317.speaker: Young Swati social media user (Facebook post)
a317.name: Young Swati social media user (Facebook post)
a317.speech: “If Beyoncé can stay Beyoncé after marriage, why can't a Swati man become a Motsa when he marries a Motsa?”

a386.speaker: Cecilia Skana, beneficiary from Mvula Village, T/A Mphonde
a386.name: Cecilia Skana
a386.title: beneficiary from Mvula Village, T/A Mphonde
a386.speech: Thanked Dodma for coming to their rescue; said the rainstorm early this month destroyed her house and some property. "I was stranded and life became difficult because I had no food, but now I have something to eat." ; She said the bag of maize will take her a long way as she dedicates her time to working in her garden and looking for other resources to repair the home.

a386.speaker: Robert Khuka, beneficiary from Chidzuma Village in T/A Mphonde
a386.name: Robert Khuka
a386.title: beneficiary from Chidzuma Village in T/A Mphonde
a386.speech: Said he had no money to buy maize: "A 50 kilogramme of maize is selling at K50 000, which I cannot raise. This maize will enable us concentrate on our gardens." ; Advised fellow beneficiaries not to sell the maize as doing so will defeat the purpose of the humanitarian assistance.

a386.speaker: Rhomatchinga Nkhata, Nkhotakota District Council disaster and risk management officer
a386.name: Rhomatchinga Nkhata
a386.title: Nkhotakota District Council disaster and risk management officer
a386.speech: Described the donation as timely: "We are pleased the 487 households finally have something to eat."

a759.speaker: Sergeant Ganizani Scale, State Prosecutor of Jali Police
a759.name: Sergeant Ganizani Scale
a759.title: State Prosecutor of Jali Police
a759.speech: Told the mobile court that Shadireki had sexual intercourse with the girl on September 12 this year; asked the court to give Shadireki a stiffer penalty considering that having sexual intercourse with a minor was a serious crime, adding that such crimes are common at Jali and Mayaka in the district.

a759.speaker: Rodrick Shadireki, 23-year-old convict
a759.name: Rodrick Shadireki
a759.title: 23-year-old convict
a759.speech: In mitigation, asked the court to be lenient with him, considering that he was epileptic on top of being a caregiver to his grandparents.

a759.speaker: Mercy Nakhumwa Bonongwe, Senior Resident Magistrate
a759.name: Mercy Nakhumwa Bonongwe
a759.title: Senior Resident Magistrate
a759.speech: Giving the sentence, also said having sexual intercourse with a minor is a serious offence that deserves a severe penalty to protect minors.

a759.speaker: Mulunguzi Senior Resident Magistrate Court (court record/proceedings)
a759.name: Mulunguzi Senior Resident Magistrate Court (court record/proceedings)
a759.speech: The court heard that the parents permitted Shadireki to have the girl as his wife; considering that fact, the court sentenced him to six years with hard labour.

a893.speaker: Hamid Khaireh Darar, President of the Association for the Promotion of Tourism and Social Development of Daasbiyo (APTDSD)
a893.name: Hamid Khaireh Darar
a893.title: President of the Association for the Promotion of Tourism and Social Development of Daasbiyo (APTDSD)
a893.speech: Said that “the information collected from some forty families will help us implement our project to improve access to water in our village.”

a893.speaker: APTDSD survey leaders
a893.name: APTDSD survey leaders
a893.speech: Urged the mothers to cooperate with the association’s surveyors by providing only accurate and truthful data, informed them that their answers would remain confidential and that each of their answers is crucial to the success of the survey, and encouraged them to answer honestly with accurate and detailed responses.

a1040.speaker: Concerned citizens
a1040.name: Concerned citizens
a1040.speech: have raised alarms over the online behavior of a U.S.-based nurse, Karimot Titilayo Ogunbayo Oyedara, following the death of Nigerian Afrobeats singer Mohbad.

a1040.speaker: Reports from individuals close to the family
a1040.name: Reports from individuals close to the family
a1040.speech: alleged that a domestic dispute involving the late singer and his partner, Omowunmi Adebanjo, preceded his death.

a1040.speaker: Karimot Titilayo Ogunbayo Oyedara, U.S.-based nurse (social media videos)
a1040.name: Karimot Titilayo Ogunbayo Oyedara
a1040.title: U.S.-based nurse (social media videos)
a1040.speech: has admitted in past videos to having a history of violent tendencies and referred to alleged incidents of violence within her family; she was most recently recorded encouraging actions against Mr Aloba and in one video suggested he should be harmed.

a1040.speaker: Karimot Titilayo Ogunbayo Oyedara, U.S.-based nurse (social media videos)
a1040.name: Karimot Titilayo Ogunbayo Oyedara
a1040.title: U.S.-based nurse (social media videos)
a1040.speech: claimed, shortly after Mohbad's death, to have spent six hours speaking with Mr Aloba, allegedly persuading him not to bury the singer prematurely, a claim she has since publicly retracted.

a1040.speaker: Community advocates
a1040.name: Community advocates
a1040.speech: have urged authorities to monitor online commentary that could endanger individuals or escalate tensions.

a1040.speaker: Concerned citizens (collective statement)
a1040.name: Concerned citizens (collective statement)
a1040.speech: “If any harm were to come to Mr. Olwabamiwo Joseph Aloba, we believe appropriate investigations must examine the impact of ongoing online statements and actions,” also calling on the Rhode Island community and relevant professional bodies to take note of concerns regarding Oyedara's conduct, stressing the need for accountability to protect the public.

a1410.speaker: Gladys Thawani Kawiya, senior official from the Catholic Agency for Relief and Development (CARD)
a1410.name: Gladys Thawani Kawiya
a1410.title: senior official from the Catholic Agency for Relief and Development (CARD)
a1410.speech: She disclosed that the assistance is being delivered under the Drought Response Project, a program funded with 170,000 Euros.

a1410.speaker: Sonia Paulino, 31-year-old recipient of the aid
a1410.name: Sonia Paulino
a1410.title: 31-year-old recipient of the aid
a1410.speech: Expressed profound gratitude to the organizations involved. "This support will significantly reduce the hardships we are facing," she said, acknowledging the impact of the aid in improving their living conditions.

a1425.speaker: Judge Brenda Neukircher, Gauteng High Court in Pretoria
a1425.name: Judge Brenda Neukircher
a1425.title: Gauteng High Court in Pretoria
a1425.speech: Dismissed the matter with costs, saying it was not in the public's interest to grant leave to appeal; in a judgment delivered virtually on Tuesday morning said that, after "careful consideration of the application for leave to appeal, the comprehensive heads of arguments", and the arguments presented before the court on Tuesday, she was convinced that granting leave to appeal was "not in the interests of justice".

a1425.speaker: Hephzibah Rajah, advocate representing the Department of International Relations and Cooperation (Dirco)
a1425.name: Hephzibah Rajah
a1425.title: advocate representing the Department of International Relations and Cooperation (Dirco)
a1425.speech: Laid out numerous fundamental reasons why her client believed the judge had erred in her judgment delivered in writing in March regarding the Cuban donation; argued that the judgment grossly interfered with the principle of the separation of powers as enshrined in the Constitution and that it was the sole prerogative of the executive, and not the courts, to conduct international relations: "The power to conduct international foreign relations is the privilege of the executive, and thus the doctrine of separation of powers was engaged when dealing with decisions made by the executive in fulfilling its functions to conduct such humanitarian assistance" ; added that when the court granted the interdict judgment in March, it usurped Dirco's rightful powers, and that alone warranted a granting of leave to appeal; further argued that the executive decision to assist Cuba with humanitarian aid had not been concluded, yet the court had found it fitting to meddle in the matter, and that such a move amounted to premature judgment, as no imminent harm could be demonstrated by the applicant AfriForum.

a1425.speaker: Hephzibah Rajah, advocate representing the Department of International Relations and Cooperation (Dirco)
a1425.name: Hephzibah Rajah
a1425.title: advocate representing the Department of International Relations and Cooperation (Dirco)
a1425.speech: Argued that Neukircher's judgment was based on arguments stumbled upon by the applicants' legal team during court proceedings but were never contained in the founding affidavit nor in the applicant's responding affidavit: "This court erred materially in its judgment, as in accepting arguments that were never in the founding affidavit or the responding affidavit fundamentally prejudiced our client who could have brought evidence to this regard."

a1425.speaker: Johan Hamman, AfriForum's legal representative
a1425.name: Johan Hamman
a1425.title: AfriForum's legal representative
a1425.speech: Argued that when it came to the issue of the separation of powers, the Constitution was the supreme law for all three arms of government, and that the court was entitled to enter into the arena and police unlawful actions - such as the rolling over of funds to finance the donation; argued that it was the respondents that had kept information from their clients, leading to the same arguments being made off the cuff during proceedings, and that a precedent had been set in law where such arguments were made, and the interdicts were granted.

a1425.speaker: AfriForum
a1425.name: AfriForum
a1425.speech: Welcomed the judgment, saying: "We are glad that the court upheld the interdict, since it is simply unacceptable, irrational and illegal for the government to squander money that could be used to solve the myriad of problems in this country."

a1539.speaker: Myriam Montrat, Canadian High Commissioner to Ghana
a1539.name: Myriam Montrat
a1539.title: Canadian High Commissioner to Ghana
a1539.speech: Said a significant portion of Ghanaians in the diaspora did not have financial connections with banks in Ghana and other investment opportunities; while advocating intensified awareness creation on investment opportunities for members of the diaspora by stakeholders, she also emphasised the need for members of the diaspora to utilise available services and resources, including Ghana's missions abroad as well as trade offices, to explore investment opportunities.

a1539.speaker: Myriam Montrat, Canadian High Commissioner to Ghana
a1539.name: Myriam Montrat
a1539.title: Canadian High Commissioner to Ghana
a1539.speech: Highlighted the exponential contribution members of the diaspora had made to the country's economy over the years: "In 2024, remittances to Ghana reached approximately $6.65 billion, exceeding the combined foreign direct investment and official development assistance" ; "This is a powerful testament to the economic strength and commitment of the Ghanaian diaspora" ; added that in Canada alone the Ghanaian-born population was estimated at over 100,000, many of whom "are professionals in government, health care, education and business. Others are entrepreneurs trading Ghanaian and African products. Yet, the full scope of the financial contributions from Diaspora to Ghana remains underreported and underutilised" ; called on stakeholders to do more "to track, measure and amplify these contributions not just as remittances but as strategic investments that drive development outcomes."

a1539.speaker: Nana Yaa Afriyie Ofori-Koree, Head of Partnerships, Sustainability and CSR at Fidelity Bank Ghana
a1539.name: Nana Yaa Afriyie Ofori-Koree
a1539.title: Head of Partnerships, Sustainability and CSR at Fidelity Bank Ghana
a1539.speech: Highlighted a paradox of Ghanaians living abroad sending billions back home as remittances while investing very little: "A recent study found that only 43 per cent of Ghanaian diaspora have savings or deposit accounts in Ghana, and even fewer (about 12-16 per cent) invest in a business or government bonds. Alarmingly, about 36 per cent of diaspora respondents reported having no formal savings or investment in Ghana at all. In other words, a third of Ghanaian professionals living overseas have no concrete ties to our financial sector" ; said that gap meant the country was missing out on a huge pool of talent and capital, and that although many Ghanaians abroad had registered interest to invest in the country, they often felt far from the process as they faced "red tapes, lack of clear information or simply the hustle of managing a portfolio while overseas," adding that "let's not overlook the trust deficit."

a1539.speaker: Nana Yaa Afriyie Ofori-Koree, Head of Partnerships, Sustainability and CSR at Fidelity Bank Ghana
a1539.name: Nana Yaa Afriyie Ofori-Koree
a1539.title: Head of Partnerships, Sustainability and CSR at Fidelity Bank Ghana
a1539.speech: Encouraged Ghanaians in the diaspora to change the narrative because banks and the government had turned the spotlight on the diaspora and lowered barriers as well as designed products with the diaspora in mind: "We have the Non-Resident Ghanaian (NRG) account – a specially designed account that lets Ghanaians abroad manage their money back home easily," explaining that Ghanaians abroad could open an account online, save in cedis or dollars, pay bills, fund investments or send money to relatives with just a few taps from anywhere in the world ; on the side of the government, she said policies were being improved to welcome diaspora investment, with regulators also making it easier for banks to innovate: "Across the sector, we see a growing ecosystem: fintech firms building diaspora-friendly apps, government programmes encouraging diaspora entrepreneurs, and even ideas like diaspora bonds being explored. These mean that if you want to invest $5,000 or $500,000 in Ghana today, there are more avenues than ever before to make it happen smoothly and securely."

a1630.speaker: Vladimir Putin, Russian President
a1630.name: Vladimir Putin
a1630.title: Russian President
a1630.speech: Said Thursday Western countries were worse hit by sanctions imposed on Moscow over Ukraine than Russia, which he insists has been resilient in the face of "external challenges" ; Western governments "guided by short-sighted, inflated political ambitions and by Russophobia, deal a much harder blow to their own national interests, their own economies and the well-being of their own citizens," Putin told a government meeting ; "We see it above all by looking at the sharp rise of inflation in Europe which is close to 20 percent in some countries," he said in televised remarks ; "It is obvious that... the continuation of the obsession with sanctions will inevitably lead to the most difficult consequences for the European Union, for its citizens" ; "Russia is confidently managing in the face of external challenges."

a1630.speaker: Vladimir Putin, Russian President
a1630.name: Vladimir Putin
a1630.title: Russian President
a1630.speech: Also welcomed the "gradual" slowdown in inflation after it surged to 16.7 percent year-on-year in March, as well as the recovery of the ruble, which is now at its strongest since the outbreak of the Ukraine crisis ; "The ruble is probably showing the best dynamics among all international currencies," Putin said.

a1957.speaker: Chawezi Sibongile Banda (‘Cha Cha’), US-based Malawian socialite and owner of Cha Cha Care Home
a1957.name: Chawezi Sibongile Banda (‘Cha Cha’)
a1957.title: US-based Malawian socialite and owner of Cha Cha Care Home
a1957.speech: Says that much as she left Malawi for the US in 2001, she has always remained connected to her motherland: “I left Malawi in 2001 when my father was an influential cabinet minister in the Bakili Muluzi administration as well as owning a newspaper giant, Nation Publications Limited. I did not leave Malawi as an economic migrant to the US but wanted to experience new challenges in life.”

a1957.speaker: Chawezi Sibongile Banda (‘Cha Cha’)
a1957.name: Chawezi Sibongile Banda (‘Cha Cha’)
a1957.speech: Says she earned her nursing license and ran a care home for a lady for ten years before setting up her own business, which she says has been success epitomized: “My business has become extremely successful and I can attribute that to God’s grace, resilience and hard work.”

a1957.speaker: Chawezi Sibongile Banda (‘Cha Cha’) (Facebook post)
a1957.name: Chawezi Sibongile Banda (‘Cha Cha’) (Facebook post)
a1957.speech: Says she has decided to support as much budding talent in the country as her team deems fit, announcing that she would fully support 14-year-old comedian Ndaziona from Chirimba Township in Blantyre by taking care of her tuition and other essential needs: “From now onwards, I have decided to assist a young comedian, Ndaziona, with her education. I feel that it is proper if I send her to a boarding school, where I will be providing all the support,” posted Cha Cha on her Facebook page ; “Talent without good education can sometimes deter one from reaching their utmost potential.”

a1957.speaker: Ndaziona, 14-year-old comedian from Chirimba Township, Blantyre
a1957.name: Ndaziona
a1957.title: 14-year-old comedian from Chirimba Township, Blantyre
a1957.speech: Expressed her gratitude saying it is a dream come true: “I promise to work hard.”

a2040.speaker: U.S. Government / United States Agency for International Development (USAID) (announcement)
a2040.name: U.S. Government / United States Agency for International Development (USAID) (announcement)
a2040.speech: Announces a new four-year program that will reduce HIV/AIDS transmission by improving access to high-quality voluntary medical male circumcision services, to be implemented by Mozambican partner ELOS, with USAID investing $28 million into the initiative over the next four years and activities focusing on men aged 15-29 in Manica and Tete provinces.

a2040.speaker: David Young, Acting USAID Mission Director
a2040.name: David Young
a2040.title: Acting USAID Mission Director
a2040.speech: Stated that "by moving the implementation of U.S. Government foreign assistance projects from international partners to local NGOs, Mozambicans will benefit from programming that is more responsive to local knowledge and has a vested interest in promoting Mozambique's development. The United States is committed to helping communities fight the spread of HIV by using proven approaches, including voluntary male circumcision."

a2114.speaker: Botswana Energy Regulatory Authority (BERA)
a2114.name: Botswana Energy Regulatory Authority (BERA)
a2114.speech: Has issued a warning against the rampant fuel smuggling especially in the north and eastern parts of the country.

a2114.speaker: Gift Bakumbi, Engineering Manager at BERA
a2114.name: Gift Bakumbi
a2114.title: Engineering Manager at BERA
a2114.speech: Told The Midweek Sun that the regulator has so far confiscated and disposed of more than 32 529 litres of illicit fuel in the current financial year, noting that this was an increase from 28 598 litres in the previous year ; said that at the end of the second quarter in 2022 they had already collected 61 127 litres confiscated from suspects who were trying to smuggle or were caught illegally exporting the fuel.

a2114.speaker: Gift Bakumbi, Engineering Manager at BERA
a2114.name: Gift Bakumbi
a2114.title: Engineering Manager at BERA
a2114.speech: "We have realised that the dispensation is being abused, where a person would cross the border multiple times in a single day carrying 100 litres claiming it is for own use. Clearly when one crosses the border on a single day many times every time crossing with 100 litres it indicates that this is no longer for own use but for some undisclosed activity" ; said that at the moment they no longer allow any export of petroleum products without a license, that they allow people to apply for a permit to export for their own use only if one uses routes that do not have filling stations immediately after the border, and cautioned members of the public that fuel export is a regulated activity that has to be done under the bounds of the law.

a2212.speaker: Joint Civil Society Anti-Corruption Initiative (JOSCAI), coalition of 10 community-based civil society organizations (petition)
a2212.name: Joint Civil Society Anti-Corruption Initiative (JOSCAI)
a2212.title: coalition of 10 community-based civil society organizations (petition)
a2212.speech: Demanded an expeditious and comprehensive implementation of the rule of law pillar of the government's ARREST Agenda, petitioning President Joseph N. Boakai to implement his promised fight against corruption and the rule of law.

a2212.speaker: Adolphus V. Banks, JOSCAI Program Manager
a2212.name: Adolphus V. Banks
a2212.title: JOSCAI Program Manager
a2212.speech: Reading the petition, demanded the government establish and ensure the full operationalization of the Witness Protection Unit, in line with section 1 of the Witness Protection Act ; called on the president to "Suspend all 959 public officials out of the total of 1,281 appointees, who according to the Liberia Anti-Corruption Commission's August 2024 report, have not declared their assets, incomes, and liabilities, thus grossly violating Part 10 of the amended Code of Conduct for public officials."

a2212.speaker: JOSCAI petition (preamble and text)
a2212.name: JOSCAI petition (preamble and text)
a2212.speech: Acknowledged that the Witness Protection Law was passed by the National Legislature providing for the establishment of the Witness Protection Unit, but that the Unit is yet to be established; spoke of making timely and speedy decisions in cases of violation of state laws and corruption involving the refusal of government officials to declare their assets upon assuming office; urged the Liberian leader to submit a Bill to the Legislature for the removal of the Statute of Limitation that prohibits prosecution of corruption cases after five years, according to Chapters 4.2 and 4.3 of the Criminal Procedure Law of Liberia; called on government to "adequately and timely fund public integrity and anti-graft institutions leading Liberia['s] fight against corruption, fraud, waste and abuse... These include, but are not limited to the Liberia Anti-[Corruption] Commission, General Auditing Commission (GAC), Liberia Extractives Industries Transparency Initiative (LEITI), Financial Intelligence Agency (FIA)." ; "Pursue an impartial and a holistic fight against corruption that sees no sacred cows or does not protect the interest of certain individuals and groups, in part through taking timely and appropriate administrative and other actions against officials of the UP-led [government] accused of grave acts of corruption and of abuse of public resources and trust."

a2212.speaker: JOSCAI petitioners
a2212.name: JOSCAI petitioners
a2212.speech: Reminded Government that the fight against corruption in Liberia remains challenged and undermined by several factors, including the weak enforcement of anti-corruption laws and policies, the absence and limitation of key institutions for dealing with corruption, and limited political will to decisively act against public officials at the center of allegations of bad governance and corruption; recalled that Liberia has signed up to key international anti-corruption frameworks such as the United Nations Convention Against Corruption (UNCAC) and the African Union Convention on Preventing and Combating Corruption (AUCPCC) as well as developing the ARREST Agenda; said "Following years of inaction by the Liberian government, it is time that actions be taken against those credibly accused of corruption and bad governance, including those sanctioned by the US government on corruption allegations and officials who have refused to declare their assets, incomes, and liabilities in blatant violation of the laws and yet sit comfortably in public offices without any reprimand".

a2212.speaker: Liberia Anti-Corruption Commission August 2024 report
a2212.name: Liberia Anti-Corruption Commission August 2024 report
a2212.speech: Found that 959 public officials out of the total of 1,281 appointees have not declared their assets, incomes, and liabilities.

a2212.speaker: JOSCAI
a2212.name: JOSCAI
a2212.speech: Says it was met with a cold shoulder, with neither the president nor any representatives from the executive coming out to receive the presentation from the campaigners.

a2212.speaker: Government of Liberia / Office of the President
a2212.name: Government of Liberia / Office of the President
a2212.speech: No government official came out to receive the petition (non-response).

a2406.speaker: Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo, Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a2406.name: Rimtalba Jean Emmanuel Ouédraogo
a2406.title: Prime Minister of Burkina Faso
a2406.speech: “We are following a logic of promoting internal, African expertise,” he declared, welcoming this initiative full of hope, both for youth employment and for the fight against insalubrity. He reaffirmed the Government’s commitment to accompany and support investors who contribute to the country’s development.

a2406.speaker: Dr Joseph Siaw Agyepong, executive chairman of Jospong Group of Companies
a2406.name: Dr Joseph Siaw Agyepong
a2406.title: executive chairman of Jospong Group of Companies
a2406.speech: Expressed his confidence in the vision of the President of Faso, Captain Ibrahim Traoré, notably his ambition to stimulate job creation and to promote a prosperous Burkina Faso; announced the imminent signing of a memorandum of understanding with the ministry in charge of the Environment, a key stage before the launch of infrastructure works ; “We do not intend to import Ghanaian workers for Burkina Faso. We are going to train young Burkinabè who will take charge of waste management in their country.”

a2479.speaker: Ahmed Magaji, Deputy Commissioner of Police of Rivers State (statement)
a2479.name: Ahmed Magaji
a2479.title: Deputy Commissioner of Police of Rivers State (statement)
a2479.speech: Indicated in a statement that the police made reasonable use of tear gas against the activists, whom he accuses of having disturbed public order.

a2479.speaker: Nigerian authorities
a2479.name: Nigerian authorities
a2479.speech: Considering that the demonstration was illegal, the Nigerian authorities set the security forces on their trail.

a2479.speaker: Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) movement
a2479.name: Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB) movement
a2479.speech: Having displayed its support for Trump from the start of the US presidential race in the hope of obtaining his backing once elected, the movement drew inspiration from the British Brexit to announce a "Biafrexit."

a2566.speaker: Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency (LDEA) (press release)
a2566.name: Liberia Drug Enforcement Agency (LDEA) (press release)
a2566.speech: In a press release, the LDEA reaffirmed its commitment to stepping up surveillance and cooperation with the authorities in order to dismantle the criminal networks operating in West Africa.

a2614.speaker: Hailemariam Dessalegn, former Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a2614.name: Hailemariam Dessalegn
a2614.title: former Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a2614.speech: On his new role serving the Ethiopian Association of Civil Engineers (EACE): “There is always enough time for any job if you use proper time management. I do have a lot more time since I have resigned as Prime Minister because I am not in such a stressful environment. Now I want to spend my time implementing a vibrant, professional association which I have learned about after several years in the civil engineering field... I believe that as the main member I need to continue to contribute. In addition to my regular membership, I need to use my influence to help the association reach its full potential and take it to the next level. For instance we need to develop professional certification. The association needs to work with the government to improve rules and regulations.”

a2614.speaker: Hailemariam Dessalegn, former Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a2614.name: Hailemariam Dessalegn
a2614.title: former Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a2614.speech: On ethics and the profession: “Most of the civil engineers in Ethiopia are young; so it is our duty to ensure their ethical and professional capacity is strengthened... Ethics isn’t something you catch all of a sudden it’s something that must be developed starting in childhood. Universities must play a major role in creating ethical citizens. However, the universities have very poor performance in this regard and I want to play a role in making things better. Ethics will make the entire nation successful. If you look at the construction industry in Ethiopia, there are some construction companies which have failed to live up to the ethical principles of the profession. The wealth of the nation did not have to be wasted because of the ethical lapses of some.”

a2614.speaker: Hailemariam Dessalegn, former Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a2614.name: Hailemariam Dessalegn
a2614.title: former Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a2614.speech: On international connections: “I am now engaged in various global initiatives. I have to choose from many requests which mean a very good opportunity to make our association internationally competitive. Establishing relationships with the American Civil Engineers Association and Canadian Civil Engineers Association helps us to gain prominence and establish relationships. Also, working with emerging associations in China, Europe and Africa is fundamental. Fortunately the president of European Civil Engineer Association is my classmate when I was in Finland that is a good opportunity for our association to establish good cooperation. Sharing knowledge with associations which have a lot of experience will help us grow and prosper.”

a2614.speaker: Hailemariam Dessalegn, former Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a2614.name: Hailemariam Dessalegn
a2614.title: former Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a2614.speech: On financing the association and foreign aid: “I believe we have to give priority to local resource mobilization and not rely on international aid. I always look at the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church as an example. They managed to build beautiful buildings in towns. They accomplished this through the support of their congregations not resources from abroad. In the construction sector, we have good resources we have not resorted to using foreign aid. Most of the class one contractors in Ethiopia are civil engineers and they are wealthy. So if they want their profession to be respected they have to contribute... The government has also given enough space so the associations including other engineering associations besides civil engineers can build our offices and lease areas... So this is the responsibility that I am planning to take with the leaders of the associations, to approach the Prime Minister and Addis Ababa Mayor to give us enough land.”

a2614.speaker: Hailemariam Dessalegn, former Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a2614.name: Hailemariam Dessalegn
a2614.title: former Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a2614.speech: On reducing waste in the construction sector: “There was a proclamation and regulation issued to govern the mobilization of construction for infrastructure. The mobilization of utilities is based on the road projects. There is also an agency established to govern the issue named the Federal Integrated Infrastructure Development Coordinating Agency. So the government noticed the matter and even established a respective body but the problem is implementation... our culture is an agrarian culture which is transitioning into an urban culture. So there is a need to change the mindset... Many matters are going to be resolved when we join the middle-income living standards and change our life style.”

a2614.speaker: Hailemariam Dessalegn, former Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a2614.name: Hailemariam Dessalegn
a2614.title: former Prime Minister of Ethiopia
a2614.speech: On corruption in the construction sector: “This is one of the major issues that always make me depressed and worrisome. The main role has to be made in society to make corruption a sin. This is not a role only to be played by the government. What the government is doing is filling the gap but other holes will erupt if this is not solved at the society level. The professional associations have to play a significant role in such a manner, and that is their main duty as other nations have experienced... If the associations are entitled to professional licensing they will regulate their members... The government is hunting the criminals but that is not a sustainable method. The sustainability has to be focused on avoiding the ethical irregularities especially corruption before it happens.”

a2614.speaker: Ethiopian government
a2614.name: Ethiopian government
a2614.speech: Admits that corruption is a major challenge in the construction sector.

a2708.speaker: Morenike Nnamdi-Nwosu, First Vice President of Ikeja Viva L'Amour Lions Club
a2708.name: Morenike Nnamdi-Nwosu
a2708.title: First Vice President of Ikeja Viva L'Amour Lions Club
a2708.speech: Said the public presentation is to let family and friends of the new president understand the enormous responsibilities of the office she now occupies and be ready to support her through the season, and also to get more service-minded people signing up to be Lions.

a2708.speaker: Col. Mabel Toyobo (rtd), incoming President of Ikeja Viva L'Amour Lions Club
a2708.name: Col. Mabel Toyobo (rtd)
a2708.title: incoming President of Ikeja Viva L'Amour Lions Club
a2708.speech: Acknowledged undertaking the task due to her passion to positively impact the underprivileged in her area of responsibility, following the Lions Club slogan of "where there is a need, there is a Lion"; pledged to society that she and her team members would deliver the goals and visions of Lionism by carrying out all Lions core projects that will impact the society at large. "Lionnism is a team work, putting in mind the 3 Ts of Time, Talents and Treasure. It's not a job I can do alone, the more the merrier. Hence more spirited and dedicated members will be encouraged to join the club to contribute their own quota."

a2708.speaker: Anastasia Gbem, immediate past President of Ikeja Viva L'Amour Lions Club
a2708.name: Anastasia Gbem
a2708.title: immediate past President of Ikeja Viva L'Amour Lions Club
a2708.speech: Expressed confidence in Toyobo's capacity to take up the mantle of leadership of the club, having known her compassion towards serving humanity long before joining the club: "She is hardworking, dedicated, kind hearted and ready to serve humanity. As a past military personnel that's been in service, being in the Lions Club is the right place for her. And I know that she will do a tremendous job in delivering service to humanity. That is why I didn't hesitate to handover to her."

a2708.speaker: Oluwakemi Eribake, District Governor, 2025/26 Lions Service Year
a2708.name: Oluwakemi Eribake
a2708.title: District Governor, 2025/26 Lions Service Year
a2708.speech: Urged the president and her team to serve with intentionality, to listen to the needs of their communities, respond with creativity and lead with humility: "As leaders, let us remember that service is most powerful when it transforms both those we serve and ourselves. May your tenure be filled with acts of kindness that bring hope; projects that spark changes and commitments that leave a legacy of true service."

a2708.speaker: Tolulope Sebanjo, immediate past District Governor of 404B2
a2708.name: Tolulope Sebanjo
a2708.title: immediate past District Governor of 404B2
a2708.speech: Recounting the immense problems in the world around us, noted that they all have a responsibility to act, to care and to serve, especially with the challenge of declining foreign aid.

a2729.speaker: Reports (unnamed)
a2729.name: Reports (unnamed)
a2729.speech: According to reports, INTPA will maintain its offices in Ghana, Senegal and Ethiopia, with a particular emphasis on migration as these countries harbour the majority of asylum seekers who arrive in Europe via irregular routes.

a2729.speaker: United States Agency for International Development (USAID)
a2729.name: United States Agency for International Development (USAID)
a2729.speech: Recently announced a 90-day suspension of its activities worldwide, including in Malawi.

a2729.speaker: Rune Skinnebach, EU Ambassador to Malawi
a2729.name: Rune Skinnebach
a2729.title: EU Ambassador to Malawi
a2729.speech: Said in an exclusive interview Tuesday that the EU had no immediate plans to downsize its delegation in Malawi, despite ongoing discussions on modernising its global network ; cautioned that future adjustments could not be entirely ruled out, as resource constraints and efficiency considerations are always factors in diplomatic operations ; “Clearly, we need to constantly think about how we can improve the effectiveness of our network, bearing in mind the European taxpayers’ money that funds it. Whether this leads to a strengthening or weakening of our presence in Malawi is completely up in the air for now.”

a2729.speaker: Rune Skinnebach, EU Ambassador to Malawi
a2729.name: Rune Skinnebach
a2729.title: EU Ambassador to Malawi
a2729.speech: Admitted that there have been internal reflections on possible restructuring of EU delegations worldwide: “What I have seen is, indeed, that as part of our permanent effort to modernise our delegation network, a number of ideas have been floated. But I can reassure you that this reflection paper has not been negotiated, nor has it been adopted by the External Action Service or the EU member states” ; said the deliberations on reducing around 100 delegations to 18 hubs remained at the preliminary stage and had not been formally discussed or adopted by key EU bodies ; noted that the EU’s new leadership, which took over in November last year, was committed to strengthening its diplomatic presence globally rather than reducing it.

a2729.speaker: Rune Skinnebach, EU Ambassador to Malawi
a2729.name: Rune Skinnebach
a2729.title: EU Ambassador to Malawi
a2729.speech: Reiterated that Malawi remained a key partner for the EU and that there were no immediate plans to alter the current engagement: “For now, we are steadfast in Malawi. We have been here since 1976 and are engaging with Malawi at an unprecedented level through budget support, biannual dialogues and high-level visits.” “There is no reason to question the EU’s commitment to Malawi at this time.”

a2729.speaker: Moses Kunkuyu, Government spokesperson (Malawi)
a2729.name: Moses Kunkuyu
a2729.title: Government spokesperson (Malawi)
a2729.speech: Said that, from the time of Covid, the world has been reshaping in many aspects ; said countries had to re-strategise and realign with objectives that suit their individual aspirations ; “With the direction that Malawi has taken in safeguarding its mineral endowment, Malawi will be the most beautiful girl in town very soon. The issue of perpetual dependence on aid will be history.”

a2729.speaker: Velli Nyirongo, economic commentator
a2729.name: Velli Nyirongo
a2729.title: economic commentator
a2729.speech: Has said if the EU plans to slash the number of its hubs, Malawi could be affected through the loss of jobs for the staff engaged at local offices, with service providers also losing business.

a2787.speaker: Enny Nyashanu, an 83-year-old grandmother and WFP food aid beneficiary in Buhera, Manicaland
a2787.name: Enny Nyashanu
a2787.title: an 83-year-old grandmother and WFP food aid beneficiary in Buhera, Manicaland
a2787.speech: “Our region is prone to drought. Aid agencies come to our rescue each year when crops fail. We cannot continue to rely on aid,” says Nyashanu.

a2787.speaker: Enny Nyashanu, an 83-year-old grandmother and WFP food aid beneficiary in Buhera, Manicaland
a2787.name: Enny Nyashanu
a2787.title: an 83-year-old grandmother and WFP food aid beneficiary in Buhera, Manicaland
a2787.speech: Says climate proofing and construction of dams for small scale farmers could be an immediate solution to wean her community off donor aid. Nyashanu told DW: “Local solutions are now needed more than ever.”

a2787.speaker: Tomson Phiri, Regional spokesperson for the WFP
a2787.name: Tomson Phiri
a2787.title: Regional spokesperson for the WFP
a2787.speech: Said the agency would run operations for eastern and southern Africa from Nairobi. “The goal is to stretch every dollar and target maximum resources to our frontline teams,” he told DW, adding the closure would not affect country operations in Southern Africa.

a2787.speaker: Tomson Phiri, Regional spokesperson for the WFP
a2787.name: Tomson Phiri
a2787.title: Regional spokesperson for the WFP
a2787.speech: “It is clear the region is going to experience more frequent droughts. There is need to invest more in irrigation infrastructure to allow people to grow food regardless of change in climate.”

a2787.speaker: UN World Food Programme (WFP)
a2787.name: UN World Food Programme (WFP)
a2787.speech: Says overall, more than 60 percent of the food it procures is used in operations in the same region it was purchased.

a2787.speaker: UN World Food Programme (WFP)
a2787.name: UN World Food Programme (WFP)
a2787.speech: Warned the “scale of this disruption underscores the far-reaching consequences of the funding pause on global food assistance efforts” and added it was still assessing the impact of vulnerable beneficiaries.

a2787.speaker: World Bank assessments
a2787.name: World Bank assessments
a2787.speech: According to World Bank assessments, countries like Zimbabwe are projected to record 6 percent economic growth driven by the anticipated agriculture recovery in 2025.

a2797.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF), World Economic Outlook published 22 April
a2797.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2797.title: World Economic Outlook published 22 April
a2797.speech: The forecasts for world economic growth in 2025 contained in the IMF's World Economic Outlook confirmed the slowdown in the momentum of the global economy, which was being felt all over the world, especially after the imposition by the United States of the so-called reciprocal tariffs. According to the IMF, the loss of momentum is expected to extend into 2026 even if the expected trade war between the US and China does not materialise.

a2797.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2797.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2797.speech: To face the current critical situation, the IMF recommends that states promote among themselves a stable and predictable environment for international trade and that they facilitate international cooperation.

a2797.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF), World Economic Outlook report
a2797.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2797.title: World Economic Outlook report
a2797.speech: The IMF also advises that at the internal level of the respective countries efforts be made to resolve the failures or insufficiencies of public policies and to reduce structural imbalances. The report says that this is essential to guarantee both internal and external stability when the international situation is more challenging, an order is disappearing and it is not foreseeable what will emerge in its place, and it is not known whom to count on when alliances, friendships and complicities are being remade.

a2797.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2797.name: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a2797.speech: Recommends stimulating growth, when it is perceptible that various factors — namely demographic ones, low birth rates and the ageing of the population, deindustrialisation and technological innovations — may be contributing to low growth and, in time, stagnation of the economy.

a2797.speaker: The New York Times (report)
a2797.name: The New York Times (report)
a2797.speech: Reported in recent days the intentions of Donald Trump's government to close several embassies and consulates in Africa, along with the ending of aid via USAID in various sectors, notably in the provision of medicines.

a2797.speaker: Prime Minister of Singapore
a2797.name: Prime Minister of Singapore
a2797.speech: In Singapore, on 8 April, the prime minister, after characterising the moment in the world as uncertain, worrying and increasingly unstable, put forward a set of measures to mitigate the impact of the changes and prepare the island, independent for sixty years and already with a per capita income of 65 thousand dollars, for the emerging economic environment. He continued his speech appealing for the country to remain “united, to pool its resources, its resilience and its determination in order to continue to be a beacon of stability, purpose and hope.”

a2797.speaker: Pope Francis
a2797.name: Pope Francis
a2797.speech: As he said, “Good also is [contagious]. Let us allow ourselves to be infected by good and let us spread good!”

a2874.speaker: Salva Kiir, President of South Sudan
a2874.name: Salva Kiir
a2874.title: President of South Sudan
a2874.speech: Has directed the Minister of Humanitarian Affairs to urgently coordinate emergency relief for flood-affected communities in the Greater Pibor Administrative Area; in response to the briefing, acknowledged the critical role of infrastructure in sustaining service delivery and pledged his administration's commitment to rehabilitating the road network in the Greater Pibor Administrative Area

a2874.speaker: Presidential Press Unit (South Sudan)
a2874.name: Presidential Press Unit (South Sudan)
a2874.speech: Said the directive came after a briefing from Greater Pibor Area Chief Administrator Gola Boyoi Gola

a2874.speaker: Gola Boyoi Gola, Chief Administrator of the Greater Pibor Administrative Area
a2874.name: Gola Boyoi Gola
a2874.title: Chief Administrator of the Greater Pibor Administrative Area
a2874.speech: Said thousands of families have been displaced by widespread flooding and called for immediate humanitarian assistance to address food, shelter, and medical needs; also raised concerns about poor road infrastructure, including the closure of the Juba-Pibor Road, which has severely disrupted the delivery of essential goods and services and worsened living conditions in the area; highlighted the need for continued dialogue to ease intercommunal tensions and promote peaceful coexistence, noting that his administration is working with local youth to maintain stability within and beyond the community

a3120.speaker: Khassim Diagne, Resident Coordinator of the United Nations System in Mali
a3120.name: Khassim Diagne
a3120.title: Resident Coordinator of the United Nations System in Mali
a3120.speech: Speaking at the ceremony, said that the floods constitute a serious humanitarian concern and that the United Nations agencies had decided to make their contributions to the populations affected by natural disasters, in support of the initiatives of the government and of Mali's humanitarian partners.

a3120.speaker: Nicolas Simard, Ambassador of Canada to Mali
a3120.name: Nicolas Simard
a3120.title: Ambassador of Canada to Mali
a3120.speech: Stressed that his country works for a win-win partnership through multifaceted support within the framework of health projects (Clef, Yellen, etc.). He welcomed the contribution of Canadian mining companies to the promotion of maternal and neonatal health, to education and to the promotion of new and renewable energies in the Kayes region. He recalled that Canada, whose partnership with Mali will continue, had granted one million dollars, or five hundred and fifty million CFA francs, in humanitarian aid to Mali.

a3120.speaker: Redouane Ag Mohamed Ali, Minister Commissioner for Food Security
a3120.name: Redouane Ag Mohamed Ali
a3120.title: Minister Commissioner for Food Security
a3120.speech: Recalled the operationalization of the Unified Social Registry (RSU), which will allow all members of the food security system to be at the same level of information regarding the situation of vulnerable populations. He recalled the actions undertaken in the regions of Gao, Bougouni, Sikasso, Koutiala and Kayes (Yelimane) on behalf of flood victims, in addition to the planning of the national programme of response to food insecurity 2024 currently being implemented.

a3120.speaker: Assa Badiallo Toure, Minister of Health and Social Development of Mali
a3120.name: Assa Badiallo Toure
a3120.title: Minister of Health and Social Development of Mali
a3120.speech: Stressed that the Kayes region had recorded 15 cases of flooding, affecting 792 households made up of 6,273 disaster-stricken people, and 6 deaths, and detailed the food and non-food assistance delivered (48 tonnes of rice, 20 tonnes of millet, 136 jerrycans of oil, 470 shelter kits, 100 NFI kits, 136 household kits, medicines and consumables, cash transfers to 1,843 households worth more than 116 million CFA francs, and school and dignity kits worth more than 201 million CFA francs).

a3120.speaker: Assa Badiallo Toure, Minister of Health and Social Development of Mali
a3120.name: Assa Badiallo Toure
a3120.title: Minister of Health and Social Development of Mali
a3120.speech: Specified that this gesture will continue through other actors for the well-being of all those affected by the floods, and took the opportunity to thank the main partners for their promptness in responding with assistance for populations in distress.

a3120.speaker: Representative of the flood victims
a3120.name: Representative of the flood victims
a3120.speech: Congratulated the government and the humanitarian partners for their assistance since the beginning of the floods and offered blessings for the country and its leaders.

a3120.speaker: Religious and customary notabilities / traditional authorities of Kayes
a3120.name: Religious and customary notabilities / traditional authorities of Kayes
a3120.speech: Thanked the Minister and her delegation for this mark of respect and consideration; hailed the success of the recent cervical and breast cancer screening campaign as well as the various donations of food and non-food items; expressed their support for the Ministry's approach of coordinating support actions for disaster-stricken populations and offered “douwaou” so that Mali may bring the transition to a successful conclusion.

a3155.speaker: Wale Edun, Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy
a3155.name: Wale Edun
a3155.title: Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy
a3155.speech: Has said that the President Bola Tinubu-led Nigerian government has enlisted the World Bank’s support in securing $50 million to support state governments in installation of metres and implementing pilot solar plants and upgrading infrastructure ; highlighted World Bank-backed initiatives such as the Power Sector Recovery Operation and the Distribution Sector Recovery Programme, saying the initiatives aimed to enhance power distribution and management systems to stimulate economic growth and development nationwide ; emphasised that the programme includes plans to deploy 3.5 million prepaid meters to improve power distribution and support tariff frameworks, market reforms, and co-financing for the Transmission Company of Nigeria’s Performance Improvement Plan ; underscored the Nigerian government’s commitment to driving economic growth by prioritizing investments in the power sector ; noted that the collaboration seeks to strengthen Nigeria’s power sector, expand energy access, foster economic growth and development, enhance job creation, and alleviate poverty, aligning with the Renewed Hope Agenda of the current administration ; reiterated President Tinubu’s administration’s dedication to revitalising the nation’s economy.

a3155.speaker: Mohammed Manga, Director of Information and Public Relations, Ministry of Finance (statement)
a3155.name: Mohammed Manga
a3155.title: Director of Information and Public Relations, Ministry of Finance (statement)
a3155.speech: A statement issued by Manga noted that the meeting aimed to explore innovative strategies for advancing Nigeria’s power sector.

a3155.speaker: Nigerian government and the World Bank (joint)
a3155.name: Nigerian government and the World Bank (joint)
a3155.speech: Affirmed their commitment to working together to achieve these objectives for the benefit of all Nigerians.

a3312.speaker: Bamidele Faparusi, chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and former member of the House of Representatives (statement by his Media Office)
a3312.name: Bamidele Faparusi
a3312.title: chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and former member of the House of Representatives (statement by his Media Office)
a3312.speech: Has opposed the proposal for the creation of more states, describing it as a ruinous action that will create chaos and economic woe ; vehemently opposed the creation of more States, saying such arrangement would cannibalize the governance structure further ; stated that adopting such strategy under an economic situation, whereby only a few states could operate frictionlessly without federal allocation would further create more economic crises like poverty, unemployment, and inability of states to provide expected social services and infrastructures ; “The National Assembly should jettison the idea of creating more states, because it will simply weaken the existing states further, polarize the country the more and increase the cost of governance” ; averred that with more states in existence, the government will be burdened financially through election of more governors, National Assembly members and appointments of more citizens that will increase the cost of governance ; “Creating more states at a time people are calling for reduction of cost of governance will be implausible With more states, you will have more governors, National Assembly members, State assembly members, Ministers, commissioners, and more Special Advisers” ; “I think it’s completely a bad idea that will create jobs for only politicians and make the citizens poorer.”

a3312.speaker: Bamidele Faparusi, chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and former member of the House of Representatives
a3312.name: Bamidele Faparusi
a3312.title: chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) and former member of the House of Representatives
a3312.speech: Backed a structural devolution of powers that will fortify the already existing states, local governments and regional commissions, signed into laws by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu to drive regionalism ; was thrilled by the creation of regional development commissions and granting of financial autonomy to the 774 local governments by President Tinubu, branding this as a game changer that will bring gradual and seamless devolution of power to states and possibly the regions ; warned Nigerians against paying lip service to the concerning issue of restructuring of governance in the country, saying the steps being taken by the current APC-led federal government should be fully supported, rather than being sabotaged ; “With the trend of things in Nigeria, what we need now is regional integration, which the Development Commission Bills signed into laws by President Bola Tinubu can easily propel, because most of the states are struggling, without the federal allocation, how many of them can survive?” ; “We should use the template of regional development commission to developing a regional governance structure that will allow for devolution of powers from the central government to the regions” ; “Everyone has been calling for restructuring and this is the time for it” ; “We fashion our own democracy after the United States of America. One state in America, like Texas, is a size of Nigeria, aside the issue of population. So, the idea of state creation is a misplaced priority, instead we should create regional government that will allow for regional integration which will accelerate our development.”

a3477.speaker: World Bank
a3477.name: World Bank
a3477.speech: The World Bank now projects ~2.0% real GDP growth in 2025, implying another year of falling income per person unless we accelerate private-sector activity and exports.

a3477.speaker: Reserve Bank of Malawi
a3477.name: Reserve Bank of Malawi
a3477.speech: The Reserve Bank of Malawi expects average inflation of ~28.5% in 2025 - better than 2024, but still a heavy drag on businesses and households.

a3477.speaker: Hannington Gondwe, CEO of the UK-Malawi Chamber of Commerce (UKMCC)
a3477.name: Hannington Gondwe
a3477.title: CEO of the UK-Malawi Chamber of Commerce (UKMCC)
a3477.speech: As the UK-Malawi Chamber of Commerce, we exist to convert intent into deals ; argues that trade and investment are "not one policy strand among many; they are the engine that will power fiscal stability, food security and inclusive growth", and sets out five immediate priorities for the new government (a "National Deal" for exporters, bankable projects, energy for industry, full use of trade access under the UK-ESA EPA, and diaspora capital and skills).

a3486.speaker: Medicines Control Agency (MCA) (press release / notice)
a3486.name: Medicines Control Agency (MCA) (press release / notice)
a3486.speech: Issued a notice on the closure of Innovarx Global Health, making claims regarding the company's operations and deeming the confiscated medications "illegal" on the basis of recent amendments to documentation requirements.

a3486.speaker: Innovarx Global Health (press release, 4 February 2024)
a3486.name: Innovarx Global Health (press release
a3486.title: 4 February 2024)
a3486.speech: Has issued a press release describing the Medicines Control Agency press release as misleading and defamatory: "We are deeply concerned and disheartened by the misleading and defamatory allegations directed at our company and our CEO, Dr. Ismail Badjie." ; "At this time, we are deliberately choosing not to engage in a public dispute with the regulator as we continue to consult with all relevant stakeholders. Our focus is on ensuring that our facility is reopened to serve the people of The Gambia."

a3486.speaker: Innovarx Global Health (press release, 4 February 2024)
a3486.name: Innovarx Global Health (press release
a3486.title: 4 February 2024)
a3486.speech: On inspection and compliance: "We cooperated with the MCA inspectors and steadfastly maintained the integrity of our operations, including the storage and transportation conditions of our medicines" ; "100% of the medications dispensed by Innovarx are sourced from the United States of America (USA). Each product that was confiscated complied with U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) guidelines, which mandate a QR code on the bottle/package to enable tracking and tracing throughout its entire supply chain."

a3486.speaker: Innovarx Global Health (press release, 4 February 2024)
a3486.name: Innovarx Global Health (press release
a3486.title: 4 February 2024)
a3486.speech: On the confiscation and public safety: "The decision by the Medicines Control Agency (MCA) to close Innovarx and confiscate medications valued at $80,000 - medications that are essential to saving lives - raises serious concerns. We affirm that all FDA-approved medications were sourced from the USA and were deemed 'illegal' by the MCA, not due to quality issues but owing to technicalities arising from recent amendments to documentation requirements." ; states that "Innovarx stands ready to engage in constructive dialogue with the MCA and other higher authorities to resolve these matters."

a3628.speaker: Anthony Chiejina, Group Chief Branding & Communications Officer, Dangote (statement)
a3628.name: Anthony Chiejina
a3628.title: Group Chief Branding & Communications Officer, Dangote (statement)
a3628.speech: Confirmed in a statement released Friday that Aliko Dangote has formally stepped down as Chairman and Director of Dangote Cement Plc, effective July 25, 2025, and that the decision is aimed at "focusing more attention" on the company's energy and industrial transformation agenda ; "The board of Dangote Cement has, therefore, announced the appointment of an independent non-executive director, Emmanuel Ikazoboh, as the new Chairman of the Board of Directors." ; "His vision and tenacity redefined not just a company, but the entire cement industry landscape by becoming Africa's largest cement producer and largest exporter of cement and clinker in Sub-Saharan Africa" ; "Dangote Cement's capacity now stands at 52.0Mta across Africa, with 35.25Mta in Nigeria alone. Two more plants — in Côte d'Ivoire and Itori — will soon push that to 61.0Mta. The company also posted a record revenue of N2.07tn in H1 2025, up from N1.76tn in the same period in 2024."

a3628.speaker: Emmanuel Ikazoboh, new Chairman of Dangote Cement Plc
a3628.name: Emmanuel Ikazoboh
a3628.title: new Chairman of Dangote Cement Plc
a3628.speech: "I am truly honoured to accept the role of Chairman of Dangote Cement Plc," he said, pledging to uphold "the highest standards of leadership and dedication."

a3692.speaker: Thandi Modise, South African Defence Minister
a3692.name: Thandi Modise
a3692.title: South African Defence Minister
a3692.speech: Has defended her attendance at an international security conference in Russia, saying South Africa would have accepted a similar invitation from the State of Israel ; responding to a question from DA MP Kobus Marais, said South Africa and Russia enjoyed cordial relations, with both countries having signed military agreements benefitting both countries: “The acceptance of the invitation was seen as a crucial step to articulate South Africa’s position on the need for the maintenance of international peace and security.” “We obey all nation states from across the continent, and we would similarly have accepted an invitation had it come from the State of Israel given the conflict ongoing there,” she added ; also told MPs South Africa should never run away from dealing with issues of toxic national interests, confirmed South Africa and Russia still enjoyed good relations, and said: “No country’s national interests are so important that it can be used to oppress other nations.”

a3692.speaker: Thandi Modise, South African Defence Minister
a3692.name: Thandi Modise
a3692.title: South African Defence Minister
a3692.speech: At the conference earlier this month, spoke tough against warmongers: “Through our own silence in action and selective morality, we have allowed warlords to reign supreme in the world and thus allowing their deadly agendas to flourish unabated. The world can no longer afford to be held to ransom by warmongers.”

a3692.speaker: Thandi Modise, South African Defence Minister
a3692.name: Thandi Modise
a3692.title: South African Defence Minister
a3692.speech: Asked about the reasons behind the war, said: “I do know that whatever it is, it must be taken right back to NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organisation) and the inability of the United Nations to intervene when it should have intervened. That is why we have been calling for a relook at the power relations in the UN [Security Council]. The big brother, little sister syndrome there … we must also be looking at the power that is vested in the countries that make up the UN Security Council. When the UN was formed, we thought that all members would be equal.”

a3692.speaker: Kobus Marais, DA MP
a3692.name: Kobus Marais
a3692.title: DA MP
a3692.speech: Put a question to the Defence Minister in the National Assembly about her trip to the international security conference in Russia.

a3870.speaker: Invited guest on an international television news network interview (unnamed)
a3870.name: Invited guest on an international television news network interview (unnamed)
a3870.speech: Responded to the effect that no one could seriously be held liable for any of the negative impacts of slavery caused by the mass displacement of entire Black populations as a result of the slave trade; went on to assert and confirm that, in fact, Black people were taken from the shores of Africa, particularly West Africa, with the full consent and cooperation of African tribal chiefs and that in the majority of cases, these chiefs were well compensated.

a3870.speaker: Russell Mmiso Dlamini, Prime Minister of Eswatini
a3870.name: Russell Mmiso Dlamini
a3870.title: Prime Minister of Eswatini
a3870.speech: Has been quick to reassure emaSwati that these criminals pose no threat to the safety and well-being of the country’s citizens, in addition to the fact that the bill for their stay in the country will be financed by the US Government.

a3870.speaker: Government of Jamaica
a3870.name: Government of Jamaica
a3870.speech: Reports have emerged indicating that the Jamaican Government has expressed surprise, to put it mildly, about Eswatini Government’s decision to enter into an agreement with the government of President Donald Trump, to accommodate prisoners from the US, one of whom is Jamaican.

a3870.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a3870.name: Donald Trump
a3870.title: President of the United States
a3870.speech: From the beginning of his presidency Trump made it clear that America’s focus would be ‘America First’.

a3905.speaker: International Energy Agency (IEA), World Energy Outlook 2021
a3905.name: International Energy Agency (IEA)
a3905.title: World Energy Outlook 2021
a3905.speech: Natural gas consumption is expected to grow, albeit at a slower pace than renewables, with an increase of about 10% by 2040.

a3905.speaker: U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA)
a3905.name: U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA)
a3905.speech: When combusted, natural gas emits about 50-60% less carbon dioxide (CO2) than coal and around 30% less than oil.

a3982.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a3982.name: John Dramani Mahama
a3982.title: President of Ghana
a3982.speech: Hinted that the Government is in the process of setting up a national airline; noted that when the time of the expression of interest from countries who had established a commitment and technical knowledge comes, Ghana would consider partnering the UAE: “And so, when we get to that stage, I know that apart from Emirates, like Dubai and several other companies, if they’re interested in partnering with Ghana, to take advantage of Ghana as an aviation hub, we’ll be willing to work with the UAE” ; recalled that when Ghana Airways started the routes from Accra to Dubai there was a small number of people who used to go to the UAE: “Today we have daily flights with Emirates between Accra and Dubai. And we appreciate that very much.”

a3982.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a3982.name: John Dramani Mahama
a3982.title: President of Ghana
a3982.speech: Encouraged more investments from the Gulf countries into Ghana and noted there were many opportunities in different sectors; said they had already seen some investors come to Ghana, citing the initial one between Abu Dhabi and the Volta River Authority which led to the Takoradi Thermal power plant (TICO); said one of the major exports from Ghana to the UAE was gold and that the Government was looking to formalize the gold trade, setting up the Gold Board to remove a lot of the non-transparency around the gold trade, in close discussions with the UAE.

a3982.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a3982.name: John Dramani Mahama
a3982.title: President of Ghana
a3982.speech: Said there were several Ghanaians working in the UAE, many under informal agreements, and that the Government was trying to set up the Ghana Labour Export programme to train young people to international proficiency in electrical engineering, carpentry, masonry, welding, construction and other areas: “Sometimes they run into trouble when they go to the UAE. So, we want to see how we can formalize that agreement so that when they go, they go legally and have all the protection they need from the UAE government.”

a3982.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a3982.name: John Dramani Mahama
a3982.title: President of Ghana
