a3982.speech: Said Ghana set up a consulate in 2011 and an Embassy in Abu Dhabi in 2017, and stated that the Ghana-UAE relation was working very well, with the Abu Dhabi Mission having oversight of several other countries.

a3982.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a3982.name: John Dramani Mahama
a3982.title: President of Ghana
a3982.speech: Expressed gratitude to the UAE for the climate change facility given to Ghana, said the UAE gave Ghana $30 million last September to fight climate change and that Ghana was in the process of utilizing that fund to support affected communities: “We know that Africa has contributed the least to climate change but is suffering with adversity from the effects of climate change” ; “And so, when friendly countries like the UAE come around to help us with our petition, it is something that we appreciate.”

a3982.speaker: John Dramani Mahama, President of Ghana
a3982.name: John Dramani Mahama
a3982.title: President of Ghana
a3982.speech: Said Ghana would also like to cooperate in the fight against terrorism, saying “terrorism is a threat to everyone in the world”; said the West Africa subregion had become a major threat for terrorists and jihadist groups, that the collapse of the regime of the late President Muammar Gaddafi of Libya brought a lot of violence into the Sahel and that when ISIS was defeated in Syria a lot of ISIS fighters found a safe haven in the Sahel, currently involved in different attacks in Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger; reiterated the need for international cooperation against terrorism in the affected countries.

a3982.speaker: Dr Abdulla Muraid Sulaiman Mohammed Al Mandoos, Ambassador of the UAE to Ghana
a3982.name: Dr Abdulla Muraid Sulaiman Mohammed Al Mandoos
a3982.title: Ambassador of the UAE to Ghana
a3982.speech: Called for the strengthening of bilateral relations between the UAE and Ghana.

a4048.speaker: US State Department
a4048.name: US State Department
a4048.speech: announced on 20 June in Washington that the two countries had initialled a peace agreement, the fruit of three days of technical negotiations.

a4048.speaker: Washington (US government)
a4048.name: Washington (US government)
a4048.speech: hails a "major breakthrough" for regional stability and economic development.

a4130.speaker: Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, Egyptian President
a4130.name: Abdel Fattah al-Sisi
a4130.title: Egyptian President
a4130.speech: Denounced the “undisciplined management” of the dam, accusing Ethiopia of harming downstream states through “unregulated” water flows decided unilaterally.

a4130.speaker: Ethiopia (government position)
a4130.name: Ethiopia (government position)
a4130.speech: Reaffirms its sovereign right to exploit its water resources and presents the dam as a pillar of its national development.

a4130.speaker: Massad Boulos, adviser to the US President for Arab, Middle Eastern and African affairs
a4130.name: Massad Boulos
a4130.title: adviser to the US President for Arab, Middle Eastern and African affairs
a4130.speech: Announced the possibility of a direct diplomatic intervention by Washington; according to him, a meeting between al-Sisi and Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, at the initiative of President Trump, would be “probable” in order to relaunch dialogue on the management of the dam; specified that the GERD file remains “strategic” for the United States, which wishes to promote a “technical and peaceful” approach to the dispute.

a4130.speaker: Ramadan Qorani, African affairs analyst
a4130.name: Ramadan Qorani
a4130.title: African affairs analyst
a4130.speech: Said this initiative “represents a positive development and a success for Egyptian diplomacy” ; said the United States has several levers over Addis Ababa: economic pressure, financial aid and security cooperation ; “The question is whether Ethiopia is really ready to engage constructively and sincerely in new negotiations.”

a4130.speaker: Several observers
a4130.name: Several observers
a4130.speech: Believe that without Ethiopian engagement no mediation will be able to overcome the deep divergences linked to the management of the waters of the Blue Nile.

a4406.speaker: Dr Jenfan Muswere, Zimbabwean Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Minister
a4406.name: Dr Jenfan Muswere
a4406.title: Zimbabwean Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Minister
a4406.speech: Said the Grain Marketing Board (GMB)’s stock currently stands at an impressive 129 149 metric tons, which is adequate to meet the needs of rural populations, ensuring that food supply remains stable, as the country braces for the next agricultural season ; “The government is committed to closely monitoring various aspects of grain supply, including import volumes, stocks at millers, import prices, and sources.” ; “This vigilance aims to eliminate any arbitrage opportunities that could disrupt our food security.”

a4406.speaker: Dr Jenfan Muswere, Zimbabwean Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Minister
a4406.name: Dr Jenfan Muswere
a4406.title: Zimbabwean Information, Publicity and Broadcasting Services Minister
a4406.speech: Said the Ministry of Agriculture, Lands, Fisheries, Water and Rural Development has proactively established 214 surveillance traps countrywide, which are crucial for early detection and management of the African Armyworm pest ; “To enhance response capabilities, the Ministry has acquired 60 trucks, one designated for each district, ensuring timely intervention against the Armyworm menace.” ; “Furthermore, 639 809 sprayers have been distributed to beneficiaries of the Presidential Input Scheme, equipping farmers with essential tools to protect their crops.”

a4620.speaker: National Commission for Science and Technology (NCST)
a4620.name: National Commission for Science and Technology (NCST)
a4620.speech: Has challenged researchers not to stop at publishing but to be innovative and bring out solutions to Malawi's challenges.

a4620.speaker: Gift Kadzamira, NCST Director General
a4620.name: Gift Kadzamira
a4620.title: NCST Director General
a4620.speech: Said as Malawi is facing challenges such as weather shocks, food insecurity and emerging health problems, researchers have to rise above the occasion ; said NCST developed a research agenda which is in line with the Malawi 2063, and that the research agenda highlights five research priorities including agriculture, health and climate change ; “Innovations through products and processes that are discovered through research should address our challenges. That can only happen if the researchers move away from publications to innovations.”

a4620.speaker: Zanele Nyoni-Wood, University of Lancaster
a4620.name: Zanele Nyoni-Wood
a4620.title: University of Lancaster
a4620.speech: Said the workshop was premised on fostering knowledge exchange, enhancing research skills and building strong networks among African and international scholars: “The workshop also aims at providing guidance on research impact, funding opportunities and career progression for early career researchers. Ultimately, it's not just about publication but the impact they are making in their communities and that is where the issue of innovation is coming from.”

a4620.speaker: Reverend Timothy Nyasulu, Unilia Vice Chancellor
a4620.name: Reverend Timothy Nyasulu
a4620.title: Unilia Vice Chancellor
a4620.speech: Said universities were there to serve societies in different areas: “We do not want just to be people of books; we want researchers for the community. We also ensure that whatever has been written is implemented.”

a4784.speaker: World Food Programme (latest figures)
a4784.name: World Food Programme (latest figures)
a4784.speech: Reveal that because of the COVID-19 pandemic the number of people suffering from hunger could double; thus, an additional 135 million people risk suffering from acute food insecurity by the end of 2020.

a4784.speaker: World Food Programme (WFP) analysis of the consequences of the pandemic on the economy and food security
a4784.name: World Food Programme (WFP) analysis of the consequences of the pandemic on the economy and food security
a4784.speech: Underlines the potential impact of COVID-19 on the world's poorest populations.

a4784.speaker: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
a4784.name: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO)
a4784.speech: Urges countries to: meet the immediate food needs of vulnerable populations; strengthen social protection programmes; maintain global food trade; keep the wheels of the domestic supply chain moving; support the capacities of smallholder farmers to relaunch food production.

a4784.speaker: UN Global Humanitarian Response Plan to COVID-19 (document)
a4784.name: UN Global Humanitarian Response Plan to COVID-19 (document)
a4784.speech: Sets out the measures to be taken to fight the virus in the world's poorest countries and to meet the needs of the most vulnerable people, particularly those facing food insecurity.

a4790.speaker: Judge Roosevelt Willie, assigned Circuit Judge at Criminal Court 'C' (ruling)
a4790.name: Judge Roosevelt Willie
a4790.title: assigned Circuit Judge at Criminal Court 'C' (ruling)
a4790.speech: Said: "The case cannot be dismissed based on the facts, circumstances and law cited above, and that Prosecution must be allowed to prove their case", and ordered the case to proceed.

a4790.speaker: Judge Roosevelt Willie, assigned Circuit Judge at Criminal Court 'C' (ruling)
a4790.name: Judge Roosevelt Willie
a4790.title: assigned Circuit Judge at Criminal Court 'C' (ruling)
a4790.speech: In his ruling, the investigation did not establish any proof of documentary evidence such as instruction from the National Security Council, or letter of request from the National Joint Security, or the FIA to defendant Samuel Tweh, for which he approved and subsequently ordered the transfer of the above-mentioned FIA accounts; the ruling further stated that on September 22, 2023, analysis of the bank statement of the FIA US operational account shows that CBL transferred the amount of US five hundred thousand as per the instruction from Samuel Tweh, and on the same day was withdrawn by Moses Cooper, acting financial Controller of the FIA.

a4790.speaker: Judge Roosevelt Willie, assigned Circuit Judge at Criminal Court 'C' (ruling)
a4790.name: Judge Roosevelt Willie
a4790.title: assigned Circuit Judge at Criminal Court 'C' (ruling)
a4790.speech: Said: "Actions undertaken by members of the National Security Reform Intelligence do not exempt them from prosecution, except the President who is immune, according the Article 61 of the 1986 Constitution, and therefore they cannot enjoy the privilege for which they must answer, and the only place to answer is at Criminal Court 'C'."

a4798.speaker: Protesters in Kinshasa
a4798.name: Protesters in Kinshasa
a4798.speech: Accuse Western governments of failing to use their influence over neighbouring Rwanda to curb a rebellion in eastern DR Congo.

a4798.speaker: Rwanda / Kigali
a4798.name: Rwanda / Kigali
a4798.speech: Denies backing the M23 rebel group ; has consistently denied that the group is backed by Rwanda.

a4798.speaker: Pepin Mbindu, protester
a4798.name: Pepin Mbindu
a4798.title: protester
a4798.speech: “The Westerners are behind the looting of our country. Rwanda doesn’t work alone, so they must leave our country,” he was quoted by Reuters news agency as saying.

a4798.speaker: Hotel Memling (Belgian-owned hotel, Kinshasa)
a4798.name: Hotel Memling (Belgian-owned hotel
a4798.title: Kinshasa)
a4798.speech: Told the BBC it had removed the flags to avoid “provoking” protesters.

a4798.speaker: United States government
a4798.name: United States government
a4798.speech: On Sunday urged its citizens in DR Congo to “keep a low profile” and “ensure your family has enough food and water should you need to stay home for several days”.

a4798.speaker: UK Foreign Office
a4798.name: UK Foreign Office
a4798.speech: Warned that protests were “likely to continue throughout the week”, and that there was a risk that foreign nationals could be “indiscriminately targeted”.

a4798.speaker: United Nations
a4798.name: United Nations
a4798.speech: On Saturday said several of its vehicles were set alight and ransacked.

a4798.speaker: Christophe Lutundula, DR Congo’s Foreign Minister
a4798.name: Christophe Lutundula
a4798.title: DR Congo’s Foreign Minister
a4798.speech: At a meeting on Sunday gave Western diplomats and UN officials an assurance that the government will protect them.

a4798.speaker: M23 rebel group
a4798.name: M23 rebel group
a4798.speech: Says it does not want to capture Goma.

a4798.speaker: United Nations
a4798.name: United Nations
a4798.speech: Calls the conflict, which has forced nearly seven million people from their homes, one of the “largest humanitarian crises in the world”.

a4798.speaker: UN experts
a4798.name: UN experts
a4798.speech: Have said that the M23 group is backed by Rwanda, which is also led by Tutsis.

a4916.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4916.name: Donald Trump
a4916.title: US President
a4916.speech: “I thought that people were jumping a little bit out of line, they were getting yippy, you know,” Trump told reporters after the announcement ; indicated that the near-panic in markets that had unfolded since his April 2 announcements had factored in to his thinking; despite insisting for days that his policies would never change, he told reporters on Wednesday: “You have to be flexible.” ; told reporters that he had been considering a pause for several days.

a4916.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4916.name: Donald Trump
a4916.title: US President
a4916.speech: Said a resolution with China was possible as well: “China wants to make a deal. They just don't know how quite to go about it.”

a4916.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a4916.name: Donald Trump
a4916.title: US President
a4916.speech: Posting on his Truth Social account, “BE COOL! Everything is going to work out well. The USA will be bigger and better than ever before!” Later, he added: “THIS IS A GREAT TIME TO BUY!!!”

a4916.speaker: Scott Bessent, US Treasury Secretary
a4916.name: Scott Bessent
a4916.title: US Treasury Secretary
a4916.speech: Asserted that the pullback had been the plan all along to bring countries to the bargaining table ; shrugged off questions about market turmoil and said the abrupt reversal rewarded countries that had heeded Trump's advice to refrain from retaliation; he suggested Trump had used the tariffs to create maximum negotiating leverage: “This was his strategy all along. And you might even say that he goaded China into a bad position.” ; declined to say how long negotiations with the more than 75 countries that have reached out might take.

a4916.speaker: Head of China's largest e-commerce association
a4916.name: Head of China's largest e-commerce association
a4916.speech: Said Chinese companies that sell products on Amazon are preparing to hike prices for the U.S. or quit that market due to the “unprecedented blow” from the tariffs.

a4916.speaker: Beijing / China (government)
a4916.name: Beijing / China (government)
a4916.speech: Has repeatedly vowed to “fight to the end” in the escalating trade war between the world's top two economies ; said it had held talks with the European Union and Malaysia on strengthening trade in response to the tensions.

a4916.speaker: Chris Turner, ING global head of markets
a4916.name: Chris Turner
a4916.title: ING global head of markets
a4916.speech: “The U.S. and China are currently in a powerplay game of brinkmanship.”

a4916.speaker: Australian government
a4916.name: Australian government
a4916.speech: Said it had rebuffed an offer from China, its top trading partner, to work together to counter the tariffs.

a4916.speaker: Richard Marles, Australian Deputy Prime Minister
a4916.name: Richard Marles
a4916.title: Australian Deputy Prime Minister
a4916.speech: “We are not going to be holding hands with China in respect of any contest that is going on in the world,” Marles told Sky News.

a4916.speaker: The White House
a4916.name: The White House
a4916.speech: Said a 10% blanket duty on almost all U.S. imports will remain in effect ; said a delegation from Vietnam met with U.S. officials on Wednesday to discuss trade matters ; on Monday, denounced a report that the administration was considering such a move, calling it “fake news.”

a4916.speaker: Canada and Japan (governments)
a4916.name: Canada and Japan (governments)
a4916.speech: Said they would step in to provide stability if needed.

a4916.speaker: Analysts
a4916.name: Analysts
a4916.speech: Said the sudden spike in share prices might not undo all of the damage.

a4916.speaker: Reuters/Ipsos survey
a4916.name: Reuters/Ipsos survey
a4916.speech: Found that three out of four Americans expect prices to increase in the months ahead.

a4916.speaker: Goldman Sachs
a4916.name: Goldman Sachs
a4916.speech: Cut its probability of a recession back to 45% after Trump's move, down from 65%, saying the tariffs left in place were still likely to result in a 15% increase in the overall tariff rate.

a4916.speaker: US officials
a4916.name: US officials
a4916.speech: Have said they will prioritize talks with other countries.

a5093.speaker: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) (press release, 9 May 2024)
a5093.name: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) (press release
a5093.title: 9 May 2024)
a5093.speech: MSF has been forced to suspend work in Madani Teaching Hospital in Sudan due to harassment and obstructions; over three months, teams in Madani Teaching Hospital have faced repeated security incidents, including looting of the hospital.

a5093.speaker: United States
a5093.name: United States
a5093.speech: Has issued a fervent appeal for all armed forces in Sudan to cease attacks immediately, amid escalating tensions and the looming threat of violence in El Fasher, North Darfur.

a5093.speaker: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP)
a5093.name: United Nations World Food Programme (WFP)
a5093.speech: The UN food agency warns that unless the people of Sudan receive a constant flow of aid...

a5093.speaker: Sudan's acting foreign minister
a5093.name: Sudan's acting foreign minister
a5093.speech: Said Sudan has recalled its ambassador from Nairobi in protest against Kenyan President William Ruto's hosting of talks with paramilitary commander Mohamed Hamdan Daglo.

a5105.speaker: Two civil servant unions (court case)
a5105.name: Two civil servant unions (court case)
a5105.speech: Brought the case to court, claiming that Trump’s orders exposed the agency’s workers abroad to undue hardship and risk. The unions also argued that the US head of state does not have the authority to close USAID without Congressional approval.

a5105.speaker: USAID sources in Maputo (anonymous)
a5105.name: USAID sources in Maputo (anonymous)
a5105.speech: Assured ‘Carta’ that the institution resumed its activities this week and employees should remain in their posts until at least Friday, February 14, awaiting the outcome of the case. However, they emphasize that not all areas of the organization have resumed activities: areas such as prevention, circumcision and gender-based violence in the health sector remain suspended.

a5105.speaker: Official confirmation (non-response)
a5105.name: Official confirmation (non-response)
a5105.speech: It was not possible to obtain official confirmation.

a5105.speaker: US State Department
a5105.name: US State Department
a5105.speech: Claims that USAID “has long strayed from its original mission of responsibly advancing American interests abroad”; the source believes that, with the suspension of funding worldwide, “it is quite clear that significant portions of USAID funding are not aligned with the fundamental national interests of the United States”.

a5117.speaker: Abdoulaye Seydou, Minister of Trade and Industry of Niger
a5117.name: Abdoulaye Seydou
a5117.title: Minister of Trade and Industry of Niger
a5117.speech: "There are thirty-one (31) trucks that have just left and four others are at the entrance to Niamey which will also come in, with a total of 1,500 tonnes of 32.5 cement," the minister in charge of Trade recalled ; noted the lack of consistency and of sufficient quantities of cement available on the ground: "We insisted on calling on the factory managers to produce more 32.5 cement. In that spirit, MCC has today deployed, exceptionally, more than 1,500 tonnes to the City of Niamey. All eighteen (18) points of sale are supplied with an average quantity of 60 to 80 tonnes minimum, and other points of sale double that, that is to say around 160 to 200 tonnes of cement for today."

a5117.speaker: Abdoulaye Seydou, Minister of Trade and Industry of Niger
a5117.name: Abdoulaye Seydou
a5117.title: Minister of Trade and Industry of Niger
a5117.speech: "We also wish to salute and express our encouragement to their partner, notably Trans Logistique, which has agreed to handle the transport of 32.5 cement at the price set by the State. We know that many players and transporters have balked and are not facilitating the delivery of 32.5 cement. It is a gesture that we wish to salute. For us this is part of a logic of being able to create the conditions, on the eve of the rainy season, for supplying all the regions with sufficient quantities of 32.5 cement. It is a special operation that concerned the City of Niamey." ; "Each week we will target one specific region and deploy all the necessary efforts so that it is supplied in sufficient quantity. This is part of a policy of equity and justice for the whole population so that everyone can have access to this 32.5 cement, in line with the will of the Head of State on this eve of the rainy season."

a5117.speaker: Abdoulaye Seydou, Minister of Trade and Industry of Niger
a5117.name: Abdoulaye Seydou
a5117.title: Minister of Trade and Industry of Niger
a5117.speech: Issued an appeal to fellow citizens to make good use of the cement: "The people for whom this cement is sold must not buy it at 55,000 FCFA and then go to other neighbourhoods or areas to create a shortage and sell it at 60,000 FCFA or 70,000 FCFA. That is not a good thing and it is a lack of civic spirit. We call on citizens to watch over the price as it is indicated," he warned.

a5258.speaker: Avelino Mondlane, president of the Red Cross of Mozambique
a5258.name: Avelino Mondlane
a5258.title: president of the Red Cross of Mozambique
a5258.speech: "Our intention is to collect as much as possible, particularly clothing and non-perishable products to guarantee that we respond to the needs of these people" ; according to Mondlane, it is difficult to define, in quantitative terms, the real needs of these people, as each day more people arrive and thus the needs increase ; "We have also assisted victims in the process of arrival by sea, as well as in the issue of shelter. Just last week, we received two European Union cargo ships with supplies" ; says the level of support has been slow, but it is arriving.

a5258.speaker: Alexandre Surikov, Russian Ambassador to Mozambique
a5258.name: Alexandre Surikov
a5258.title: Russian Ambassador to Mozambique
a5258.speech: Said that "this gesture shows that Russian companies are also concerned about the situation in Mozambique and we promise to continue with similar initiatives."

a5258.speaker: Evgeny Volosov, chairman of the Board of Directors of Tazetta Resources
a5258.name: Evgeny Volosov
a5258.title: chairman of the Board of Directors of Tazetta Resources
a5258.speech: Said this is not the first time that the Russian company has supported Mozambique: "As part of our social responsibility, we have already invested in the areas of health and education. An operating room in the District Hospital of Pebane was rehabilitated, a medicine warehouse was built from scratch in the same hospital and we have already rehabilitated many schools in Pebane and in Mocubela districts."

a5517.speaker: Ernest Mkhonta, Managing Director of the Eswatini Electricity Company (EEC)
a5517.name: Ernest Mkhonta
a5517.title: Managing Director of the Eswatini Electricity Company (EEC)
a5517.speech: “As we look ahead to the 2024/25 financial year, we anticipate energy sales reaching 1,181 GWh, which is crucial for sustaining our operations and meeting the growing electricity demand.”

a5517.speaker: Ernest Mkhonta, Managing Director of EEC
a5517.name: Ernest Mkhonta
a5517.title: Managing Director of EEC
a5517.speech: “Our monthly sales revenue averages E252 million, but with procurement costs soaring, we are facing a cash position that will be highly overdrawn in the coming months.” ; “While local power generation stands at 280 GWh, our dependence on imports makes us vulnerable to fluctuations in global energy prices.”

a5517.speaker: Ernest Mkhonta, Managing Director of EEC
a5517.name: Ernest Mkhonta
a5517.title: Managing Director of EEC
a5517.speech: Acknowledged the government-approved tariff increases (8 per cent for FY2025/26 and 7 per cent for FY2026/27) as insufficient: “The approved tariff increases do not align with our operational costs and the necessary investments in infrastructure.”

a5517.speaker: Ernest Mkhonta, Managing Director of EEC
a5517.name: Ernest Mkhonta
a5517.title: Managing Director of EEC
a5517.speech: “We recognise the importance of our large customers and are dedicated to providing them with reliable electricity, which is essential for their operations and the overall economic growth of the country.”

a5579.speaker: Kamilou Arouna, Vice-President of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCI-Bénin)
a5579.name: Kamilou Arouna
a5579.title: Vice-President of the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Benin (CCI-Bénin)
a5579.speech: Thanked the actors of Benin’s private sector for the interest shown in this instrument of economic integration: “Our everyday commercial operations do not take place without obstacles. Even more so for those focused on cross-border trade… This meeting marks a relaunch of the Trade Obstacles Alert Mechanism, a tool initially created for the member countries of UEMOA but which today is extended to all ECOWAS countries for the resolution of obstacles to intra- and extra-regional trade…” ; said that companies, states and regional organisations all stand to gain from smooth trade because it contributes to economic development and to the strengthening of regional integration, and urged all stakeholders to engage in frank collaboration for the effective removal of the non-tariff barriers that hinder regional and international trade.

a5579.speaker: Justin Bayili, senior trade adviser of the USAID support programme for ECOWAS agricultural policy
a5579.name: Justin Bayili
a5579.title: senior trade adviser of the USAID support programme for ECOWAS agricultural policy
a5579.speech: Emphasises the importance of working with all actors facilitating economic exchange in order to resolve non-tariff barriers: “We have got into the habit of leaving the resolution of the problems we encounter on our corridors to public actors, forgetting that we ourselves, as private actors, have our own responsibilities in resolving these problems, particularly non-tariff measures” ; specifies that the trade obstacles alert mechanism gives private actors the opportunity to report the obstacles they encounter so as to enable public actors to find appropriate solutions.
